r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding:
FAIL. BOM defect: correct, complete, well-evidenced (see r3/r5). D3 defect: the
Commander's reading is correct for the LITERAL symptom it was built to fix, but the
fix has an independently-confirmed regression on the DOMINANT real docstring shape
in this corpus, and that regression is worse information loss than the original bug.

=== Q1: is "summary = first paragraph, ends at first blank line (PEP 257)" the right
reading of D3? ===

Partially. It correctly fixes the demonstrated symptom: a short summary sentence
wrapped across 2 physical lines, followed by a blank line and a formal body (e.g.
Args:), used to be cut mid-sentence at the newline. `_first_paragraph` now joins
those lines and stops at the blank line -- verified correct against
`_git_rev_parse`-shaped and Args:-shaped fixtures.

But I checked real docstrings in this repo per the handoff's own instruction (Q1,
last sentence) and found the fix creates a NEW, larger regression for the shape
that actually dominates this codebase: a single dense multi-line paragraph with NO
blank line at all. A grep+AST scan of scripts/**/*.py alone found 132 docstrings
matching this shape (>=2 physical lines, no blank line, joined length >160 chars) --
e.g. scripts/agent_work_root.py:_git_rev_parse (3 lines, no blank line, 219 chars
joined), scripts/checklist_engine.py:_glob_to_regex (504 chars joined).

For this shape:
  OLD (baseline, pre-g8): summary = first physical line only (short, no truncation
    needed); body = doc_body_of (everything after line 1), UNTRUNCATED. Reader lost
    only the first line's worth of continuity between summary and body -- the
    original D3 symptom -- but every word of the docstring was still on the page.
  NEW (06fbc138): since there is no blank line, the ENTIRE docstring becomes "the
    first paragraph" -> the whole thing is joined into `summary`, hard-truncated to
    160 chars at the emit call sites (summary[:160]), and `doc_body_of` returns
    None (nothing follows the blank line, because there is no blank line). Every
    character past 160 is now GONE from the page with no indication more existed --
    not moved to body, not marked with an ellipsis, just dropped.

Confirmed directly against the actual generated pages in this worktree (map/ was
rebuilt post-fix at 2026-08-08 17:57, 4 minutes after the 06fbc138 commit):
  map/scripts.agent_work_root/_git_rev_parse.md line 8 ends mid-word:
    "...and lets OSError (g" -- the source docstring's own tail ("git absent / bad
    cwd) propagate -- both caught by the caller.") is gone, and no body section is
    rendered at all.
  map/scripts.checklist_engine/_glob_to_regex.md line 8 ends mid-clause:
    "...a single `*` matches within one segment (no `/`?" -- same pattern, same
    total loss, same silent truncation.

This directly contradicts DESIGN_SPEC.md's own stated intent for the summary field
(line 129, the redundancy rule): "DO carry the structural summary that saves
opening the file at all... signature and kind stay, they were the trial's measured
wins." A summary that silently amputates the back half of the only real content on
common pages does not save the reader from opening the file -- it actively misleads
them into thinking that's all there is.

I independently confirmed (by direct execution, not just reading) that truncation
IS applied after the join, not before -- the code is internally consistent with
what it does. The defect is not a coding bug; it is that the chosen RULE ("no blank
line = the whole docstring is one paragraph, hard-cut at 160, nothing recoverable
in body") is the wrong rule for this codebase's actual docstring population, which
this review's own Q1 explicitly asked me to check.

=== Q6: is the page-content change an improvement everywhere? ===

No. It is a clear improvement for the wrapped-summary+blank-line+body shape (the
demonstrated fixture case). It is a regression for the no-blank-line long-paragraph
shape, which my scan shows is several times more common in this repo's own source
(132 hits in scripts/ alone vs. the handful of Args:-style docstrings). Net effect
on the corpus this tool actually indexes is not unambiguously positive.

=== Recommended fix (small, does not reopen the whole gate) ===

When `_first_paragraph` finds no blank line, the current code sets body=None and
lets the summary emit sites truncate the whole doc to 160 chars with total loss of
the remainder. Either: (a) when no blank line exists, treat text past the 160-char
cut as the body (so nothing is silently dropped -- it just moves from summary to
body, symmetrical with the blank-line case), or (b) keep the hard truncation but
mark it explicitly (e.g. append an ellipsis) so a reader knows content was cut,
matching the honesty posture CREW_CONTEXT.md asks for elsewhere ("fail visibly
rather than emit plausible wrong output"). (a) is more consistent with the existing
design (body already exists as a channel for "the rest of the docstring") and
requires no new field.

This is a candidate eleventh Commander/crew error this run, if it holds: not the
BOM fix (correct), not the literal wrapped-summary-cut-mid-sentence fix (correct),
but the unstated assumption that "no blank line => the whole docstring is safely
truncatable" -- which is false for the majority of this repo's own docstrings.

r3-evidence.finding:
FAIL. Three of four boundary cases the handoff named are tested and I independently
confirmed they can fail; the fourth is untested despite being explicitly required.

=== Q2: do the new tests have teeth? YES, confirmed by direct mutation ===

I reverted `_first_paragraph` in scripts/code_map/extract.py to a naive line-based
split (paragraph = lines[0], body = "\n".join(lines[1:])) -- the exact pre-fix
shape -- and re-ran `python -m pytest tests/test_code_map.py -k "bom or docstring"
-q --color=no`. Result: 2 of 8 failed, 6 passed (not 8/8 green). The two failures
were `test_wrapped_summary_is_first_paragraph` (the core defect test) and
`test_wrapped_summary_no_body` (boundary case 2) -- both go RED on this mutation,
matching the commit message's claim. `test_one_line_docstring_has_no_body` and all
BOM tests correctly stayed green (a one-line docstring has nothing to wrap, so line-
split and paragraph-split agree -- that test isn't meant to catch this mutation).
Restored via `git checkout -- scripts/code_map/extract.py`; confirmed clean via
`git diff --quiet`. This mutation is not the crew's own falsifier (I did not read
their break-test script before writing mine) -- an independent attack, and it
caught the defect.

=== Q3: boundary cases -- 3 of 4 covered, 1 missing entirely ===

Handoff (g8-remediate.md and this review's own Q3) names four boundary cases:
1. One-line docstring, body None -- COVERED (test_one_line_docstring_has_no_body),
   passes at HEAD.
2. Wrapped summary, no blank line, no body -- entire thing is the summary, body
   None, remainder must not leak into body -- COVERED
   (test_wrapped_summary_no_body), and I confirmed above it goes RED under my
   mutation.
3. Wrapped summary + blank line + Args: -- COVERED
   (test_wrapped_summary_is_first_paragraph), confirmed RED under my mutation.
4. First paragraph over 160 chars, truncation applies after joining, not before --
   NOT COVERED. No test in tests/test_code_map.py asserts this. Grepped the whole
   test file for "160" and "truncat" -- zero hits outside an unrelated stale-tag
   test.

I verified case 4's underlying behavior is actually correct by direct execution
(doc_summary_of returns the full 216-char joined paragraph untruncated; each of the
three emit call sites then applies `summary[:160]` -- truncation genuinely happens
after the join). So this is not a functional bug, but it IS a real evidence gap:
the remediation handoff explicitly asked for a test on this case
("Watch the boundary cases... A docstring whose first paragraph exceeds 160
characters -- truncation still applies, after joining") and this review's own Q3
explicitly asks to confirm all four are covered and each can fail. One was silently
dropped with no note in either RESULT document. It is also the boundary case most
directly connected to the r1-handoff finding: a test built against a REAL (not
synthetic) >160-char no-blank-line docstring would likely have surfaced the body=
None-and-truncated-with-no-recovery behavior this review flags as a regression.

=== Q4: BOM fixture -- genuine bytes, confirmed RED without fix ===

Read tests/fixtures/bom_corpus/bom_sample.py as raw bytes directly (not via the
filename): first three bytes are b'\xef\xbb\xbf', the real UTF-8 BOM. Reverted BOM
stripping in scripts/code_map/extract.py (removed both `src.lstrip('﻿')`
lines) and re-ran `-k bom`: BOMParsingTests.test_bom_file_can_be_extracted goes RED
("BOM file should parse successfully (table non-None)" -- AssertionError, table is
None). Restored via `git checkout --`, confirmed clean via `git diff --quiet`. This
repo genuinely has zero BOM files outside the fixture (confirmed earlier by the
Commander and not re-disputed here), so the fixture is the only way this check can
ever go red, and it does.

=== Q5: checks.py find -- complete, no other second-parse site missed ===

Grepped scripts/code_map/*.py for every `ast.parse` call site: exactly three exist
in the whole module -- extract.py:371 (build_table), extract.py:1282 (run), and
checks.py:246 (SourceScan). All three now strip the BOM (confirmed by reading each
site in the current tree). The two other file-reads in checks.py (line 139 and 388)
read already-generated .md map pages, not corpus source files, so they are
correctly out of scope for this defect -- verified by reading their surrounding
code (MapModel.text and no_empty_pages).

r7-recheck.title: Attempt-2 recheck: overflow-preservation fix at c385f467
r7-recheck.imperative: Verify the remediation-2 fix (commit c385f467) that resolves r1-handoff/r3-evidence's regression finding: does no-blank-line overflow past 160 chars now route into body instead of being dropped, is the invariant held for EVERY shape (not just the demonstrated case), do the new tests have teeth, and does the original short-wrapped-summary case still work. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r7-recheck.finding:
FAIL. The demonstrated regression (no-blank-line dense paragraphs) is genuinely
fixed and well-tested. But the stated invariant -- "no docstring content is ever
dropped without appearing somewhere" -- is NOT held everywhere: I found a live
counter-example in the sibling code path, affecting real docstrings in this repo
right now.

=== Q A: is the invariant held everywhere? NO -- found a live counter-example ===

Reverted only the new overflow branch (the `elif paragraph and len(paragraph) >
160` block in _first_paragraph) and re-ran the closing selector: exactly 1 test
fails (test_dense_paragraph_over_160_chars_no_blank_line, 221 != 160), the other 8
stay green. Restored via `git checkout --`, confirmed clean via `git diff --quiet`.
So the shipped fix does what it claims for the no-blank-line case, and the new test
has real teeth (Q C, answered here too).

Boundary probes around the 160-char cut (exact-160, exact-161, multi-byte/em-dash
straddling every position 157-162) all reconstruct byte-for-byte/codepoint-for-
codepoint identical to the source paragraph when summary+body are concatenated --
Python string slicing is codepoint-safe, no character is split, duplicated or lost
at the seam in any of these cases. This part of the invariant holds cleanly.

BUT: the fix only patches the NO-BLANK-LINE branch of _first_paragraph. The
BLANK-LINE branch -- the ORIGINAL D3 shape this whole gate started from, a wrapped
summary followed by a blank line and a body (e.g. Args:) -- still truncates the
summary to 160 chars at the emit call sites with NO equivalent overflow-preservation
when the first paragraph (the text before the blank line) itself exceeds 160
characters. I constructed this directly: a docstring whose first paragraph
(pre-blank-line) is 216 chars, followed by a blank line and "Args:\n    x: y."
doc_summary_of returns the full 216-char paragraph (correct, matches the paragraph-
join fix); but the emit-site truncation (`summary[:160]`) drops the last 56
characters ("one hundred and sixty characters in total length easily."), and
doc_body_of's body is only "Args:\n    x: y." -- the dropped summary tail is
NOWHERE. Confirmed programmatically: `lost text in body? False`.

This is not hypothetical. I scanned scripts/**/*.py for docstrings WITH a blank
line whose first paragraph alone exceeds 160 chars: 54 real instances (e.g.
scripts/checklist_engine.py:_rail_position, :_rail, :repo_revision;
scripts/apply_episode_delta.py:commit, :apply_retirement, :write_plan). Checked
the already-regenerated real page for one of them --
map/scripts.checklist_engine/_rail_position.md -- and the loss is live, right now:
the summary line ends mid-word ("...its ") and the body section starts directly
with the bullet list ("- \`\`n == 0\`\`..."); the connecting clause ("head
(\`\`remaining[0]\`\`) is the active gate.") from the source docstring is gone from
the page entirely, not relocated to body. Same defect class as the r1-handoff
finding this pass was built to close, in the sibling branch of the exact function
that was supposed to close it.

=== Q B: named pages + broader sample -- clean for the fixed (no-blank-line) case ===

map/scripts.agent_work_root/_git_rev_parse.md: tail restored ("...git absent / bad
cwd) propagate -- both caught by the caller." now appears in a body section).
map/scripts.checklist_engine/_glob_to_regex.md: tail restored in full. Sampled 4
more of the 132 no-blank-line entities at random (seed 42):
_condition_open, _stamp_date, _read_events, _supersede_evidence -- all four show
the previously-lost tail now present in a body section below the summary. The
no-blank-line class is genuinely fixed across the sample I checked.

=== Q C: does the new test have teeth? YES (see Q A above) ===

Confirmed by direct mutation: reverting the overflow branch makes exactly
test_dense_paragraph_over_160_chars_no_blank_line go RED (221 != 160), the other 8
selector tests unaffected. Not a check that cannot fail.

=== Q D: does the original short-wrapped-summary+blank-line+Args case still work? YES, when short ===

Re-ran the original fixture shape (summary ~122 chars after joining, wraps 2
physical lines, blank line, Args: block): summary = full 122-char joined sentence,
body = "Args:\n    x: parameter." -- correct, unaffected by this pass, matches the
first remediation's fix. But Q A shows this same shape breaks again once the
summary itself exceeds 160 chars before the blank line -- the two cases are not
independent; D and A overlap exactly at that boundary.

=== Mechanical checks, still green ===
Closing selector `-k 'bom or docstring'`: 9 passed (matches claimed count, up from
8). `python -m scripts.code_map check --root .`: 7/7 ok. Diff scope: exactly
scripts/code_map/extract.py + tests/test_code_map.py, both in allowed scope,
matches g8-remediate-2.md's stated scope.

=== Recommended fix, small, scoped to this same function ===
Apply the identical overflow-preservation logic already written for the
no-blank-line branch to the blank-line branch: when the paragraph before the blank
line itself exceeds 160 chars, route ITS overflow into body too (prepended to
whatever body already follows the blank line, e.g. via body = overflow + "\n\n" +
existing_body), rather than letting the emit-site `summary[:160]` silently drop it.
This does not touch the no-blank-line fix, the BOM fix, or the paragraph-join
mechanism -- all three remain correct.

r8-recheck.title: Attempt-3 recheck: unified overflow logic at 1f2b57ab
r8-recheck.imperative: Verify the remediation-3 fix (commit 1f2b57ab) that unifies overflow-preservation across both branches of _first_paragraph. Probe the invariant against shapes the crew would not think of (empty/whitespace/blank-only docstrings, exact boundary offsets, multi-byte straddle, CRLF, huge body). Confirm on real regenerated pages, not just the store. Check whether the new tests (including any invariant test) have real teeth by reverting and observing what goes red. Judge the branch-collapse. r8-recheck.finding:
FAIL. The underlying CODE is now correct -- I could not find a shape where the
invariant actually breaks, after extensive adversarial probing. But the SHIPPED
TESTS meant to prove this are checks that cannot fail against the exact regression
this pass exists to prevent, confirmed by two independent mutations. Per this
repo's own CREW_CONTEXT.md rule ("a check that cannot fail is indistinguishable
from one that passed"), that is a real defect in required evidence, not a
nitpick, and it is squarely what this recheck's Q C asked me to verify.

=== Q A: is the invariant real, or true only of the four hand-picked shapes? ===

Genuinely real, as far as I can push it. Probed, against the ACTUAL shipped code
(not the tests -- direct calls to doc_summary_of/doc_body_of), every shape named
in the recheck brief plus more: no docstring at all, whitespace-only, all-blank-
lines, leading blank line before text, multiple consecutive blank lines, exact
159/160/161-char boundaries with AND without a blank line, a multi-byte character
(em-dash) straddling the cut at every position 158-161 with a blank line present,
Windows CRLF line endings on a long first paragraph, and a huge (3800+ char) post-
blank-line body. Checked each with a CHARACTER-EXACT reconstruction test (not a
word-split test -- my first pass at this used word-splitting and produced false
positives on cases like "x"*161 with no internal whitespace, where a "lost word"
is actually just a mid-string split with zero character loss; redone correctly).
Zero content loss found anywhere in this battery. The invariant holds in the
actual code.

Also confirmed: the emit sites' `summary[:160]` is now a harmless no-op double-
truncation, since `_first_paragraph` already caps the paragraph at 160 before
`doc_summary_of` returns it -- consistent with the commit message's own claim.

=== Q B: does the invariant survive to real rendered pages? YES, on every sample checked ===

`map/scripts.checklist_engine/_rail_position.md` -- the page that showed the loss
last round -- now reads correctly: the connecting clause ("head (``remaining[0]``)
is the active gate.") is back, flowing straight into the bullet list body. Sampled
5 MORE real entities from the 54-item blank-line/long-first-paragraph list (seed 7:
raw_record, repo_revision, enumerate_episode_ids, _adjudicate_orphan,
_remove_superseded) -- checked 3 of them directly
(map/scripts.gauge_reader/raw_record.md, map/scripts.checklist_engine/
repo_revision.md, map/scripts.run_skill_eval/_adjudicate_orphan.md): all three
read as continuous, complete text from summary into body, including
repo_revision.md's very long (multi-paragraph) body rendering in full. Re-checked
map/scripts.agent_work_root/_git_rev_parse.md (the original no-blank-line
regression page): still correct, no new regression for that class. map/ is fresh
-- rebuilt 62 seconds after commit 1f2b57ab, confirmed by mtime.

=== Q C: do the new tests have teeth? NO -- two independent mutations both stayed green ===

This is the material finding. Two mutations, each targeting exactly the defect
this pass exists to fix:

Mutation 1 (revert the whole fix to the remediation-2 shape -- blank-line branch
does not truncate/preserve overflow internally, same as the code that was BLOCKED
last round): ALL 11 selector tests, including both new tests
(test_long_first_paragraph_with_blank_line_and_body,
test_all_shapes_preserve_complete_content) and all 4 of the latter's subTests,
stayed GREEN. Restored via `git checkout --`, confirmed clean via `git diff
--quiet`.

Mutation 2 (surgical: keep the 160-char truncation, but drop the summary-overflow
text from body -- i.e. body = post_blank_body only, discarding the overflow that
should be prepended): only the OLDER remediation-2 test
(test_dense_paragraph_over_160_chars_no_blank_line) went red, because it happens
to assert body is not None in a shape where post_blank_body is always None. BOTH
of the two tests specifically written THIS pass for the blank-line-overflow case
stayed GREEN even with the overflow text silently dropped. Restored, confirmed
clean.

Root cause, read directly in the test source: both new tests gate their

BLOCK (attempt-3) -- code correct, evidence deficient. Commit 1f2b57ab's fix
genuinely holds the invariant "no docstring content is ever dropped" -- verified
with an adversarial battery of shapes (empty/whitespace/blank-only docstrings,
exact 159/160/161 boundaries with and without a blank line, multi-byte em-dash
straddling the cut, CRLF endings, huge bodies) using character-exact
reconstruction, and confirmed on 4 real regenerated pages including the one
(_rail_position.md) that showed the loss last round. The branch collapse is right
and removes the drift risk that produced two consecutive prior findings.

But the two tests written THIS pass to guard the fix
(test_long_first_paragraph_with_blank_line_and_body,
test_all_shapes_preserve_complete_content) are checks that cannot fail against
the exact regression they exist to catch -- confirmed by two independent
mutations, both restoring prior BLOCKED states of the code, both leaving all 11
selector tests green. Root cause: both tests gate their real assertions behind
`if summary and len(summary) == 160:`, which is false when the bug is present
(summary is untruncated), so the guard skips straight past the assertions that
would have caught it; and even when the guard fires, neither test checks for the
overflow TEXT specifically, only that body is non-None / contains "Args:".

This is exactly the failure mode this pass's own brief flagged as the central
risk ("an invariant test that cannot fail is the worst of both worlds"), and
exactly what this repo's own CREW_CONTEXT.md names as the discipline that most
often separates an accepted change from a reworked one: "a check that cannot fail
is indistinguishable from one that passed."

Fix is test-only, small, and does not touch production code: remove the
conditional gate, assert len(summary) == 160 unconditionally, and assert the
overflow text itself (not just body's non-nullness) is present. Full reasoning in
r8-recheck's finding.
